reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Alan Henry fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 30-45 feet over trees with minnows.
reports.by: Randy Britton, The Bait Shop, Post, Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Arlington fishing report
reports.text: Bass will be keying in on shad baits like a crankbait and rattle trap. Crappie will be related to larger piles of wood in schools.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Austin fishing report
reports.text: Bass are really keyed in on small bait fish out in the river channel.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bastrop fishing report
reports.text: Bass should be in the reeds and shallow grass hitting Texas rigs, or squarebill crankbaits.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bob Sandlin fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on minnows in river channels to the Highway 21 bridge and in secondary depressions on timber in 20-40 feet of water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bois d'Arc fishing report
reports.text: The morning bass bite has slowed due to weather, but mid-morning has been good on swim jigs, chatterbaits and spinnerbaits around any grass you can find 2-4 feet. Crappie are good on minnows or jigs midlake in the river channel from the 897 bridge to the dam. Targeting crappie can be tough on windy days. Crappie are slow.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Braunig fishing report
reports.text: Water stained; 74 degrees; Fishing remains slow across the lake, with redfish, black bass, stripers, and catfish all showing limited activity.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bridgeport fishing report
reports.text: Fishing patterns remain consistent except the crappie bite has slowed to fair due to the cold front. Target crappie in 10-25 feet of water on docks, and offshore brush piles with minnows or jigs. Largemouth bass are good using topwaters on banks in the morning or for deeper schooling fish. White bass and hybrids are fair on main lake humps and points with topwaters, slabs or trolling with deep crankbaits. Report by Jack Pellegrini, Lake Bridgeport Crappie Guide Service.
reports.by: Jack Pellegrini, Lake Bridgeport Crappie Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brownwood fishing report
reports.text: Black bass to 8 pounds are good in 13-28 feet of water on Alabama rigs, and along the shoreline in 3-8 feet with a bladed jig, crankbait or jigs. Crappie are excellent to 12 inches on minnows and jigs on the main lake scattered brush piles in 10-15 feet.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Buchanan fishing report
reports.text: Vertical jigging has produced the best action with �½ ounce to 1 ounce slab spoons.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Caddo fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are fair on flukes, frogs, buzzbaits and chatterbaits around the shallow edge of the grass and pads, or rattle traps and shallow running crankbaits in the deeper water where the grass is not thick. It will take some cooler nights to drop the water temperature into the 50s for the black bass to bite to improve to good. Come early for bass then as the bite slows shift the focus to chase white bass in the river system.
reports.by: Vince Richards, Caddo Lake Fishing & Fellowship

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Calaveras fishing report
reports.text: Redfish, black bass, and stripers continue to be slow, with limited activity reported across most areas.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Canyon Lake fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are good on the deep edge of the hydrilla slowly working a weightless worm. Crappie are slow.
reports.by: Tyler Stanley, Game on Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cisco fishing report
reports.text: Crappie action is slowly improving on brush and timber in 12-20 feet using minnows. Bass reports are light, but a few are moving shallow on warmer afternoons and hitting spinnerbaits and squarebills around rocks.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Comanche Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass numbers are excellent with many anglers bragging on 100 fish days with an occasional fish to 6 pounds.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Conroe fishing report
reports.text: Bass are biting well along edges, with rattle traps, creature baits, and cranking wind-blown points around shad schools proving effective. Crappie are producing nice catches on structure in 13-28 feet, with minnows working best and hair jigs close behind. Hybrids remain scattered and schooling on flats in 14-34 feet, hitting slabs, spoons, and shad, with many juvenile fish mixed in, so check the tooth patch for proper identification.
reports.by: Brad Doyle with Bradley’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cooper fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow and difficult to find.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cypress Springs fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow and easily spook.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Dunlap fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good on spinnerbaits early along the banks and docks, but the bite slows by late morning. Crappie are slow with minnows.
reports.by: Lee Johnson and Kenneth Linder, local anglers

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Eagle Mountain fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on jigs and minnows around boat docks and pushing shallow due to water temperature. Black bass are fair on spinnerbaits and jerkbaits. White bass are fair on slabs in open water.
reports.by: Captain Bobby Mann, Catch a Dream Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Falcon fishing report
reports.text: Crappie fishing is also improving, with anglers finding fish on isolated vertical timber in 15-30 feet. Alligator gar bowfishing and rod-and-reel action have slowed, and no recent bass reports were available.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fayette fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow in shallow water with rattletraps and spinnerbaits, or in 12-15 feet of water on Carolina rigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fork fishing report
reports.text: The morning bass bite has slowed due to the weather changes. Black Bass are feeding in the backs of creeks and coves. Cooler nights have dropped water temperatures and bass are cruising the shallows. Streamers are enticing bass early and late in the day. Lake Fork crappie fishing is about as hot as it has ever been going into the last week of November. Fast limits of crappie can be caught off all kinds of structure. The lake has tons of keeper sized black crappie congregated on brush piles, tire reefs, underwater bridges, regular bridges, road beds, humps, points, ledges and timber. Lots of big white crappie are on deeper timber and some brush piles in 14-40 feet of water. Crappie will bite…

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Georgetown fishing report
reports.text: Bass are feeding up for the winter chasing shad. Target bass on points casting small shad imitation baits into the schools.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Graham fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on minnows in brush in 12-14 feet of water. Crappie and bass are feeding on shad. Bass are good on crankbaits on main lake points.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granbury fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are good to 4 pounds on soft plastics near weeds and laydowns. Some good topwater action for largemouth bass is good near schooling sandbass and on main lake points and flats. Best black bass reports come from the area near town and in the river above Granbury. Crappie action remains good to excellent on small jigs and minnows fished near standing timber and bridge pilings.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are biting well on drains, points, docks, and riprap banks on the south end, with squarebills, shallow crankbaits, and spinnerbaits producing early, followed by Texas-rigged worms and grubs near structure as fish transition. Crappie are steady in the East Fork on brush and channel-related cover in 12-14 feet, with live minnows and silver or white hand-tied jigs working best. 12 pet spoons, then vertical jigging slabs once schools are located.
reports.by: Captain Zackary Scott, Zack Attack Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Jacksonville fishing report
reports.text: Bass were biting on deeper brush and structure with Texas rigged big worms and jigs. Spotted bass were biting wacky worms and jigs around docks.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Joe Pool Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass will be keying in on shad baits like a crankbait and rattle trap. Crappie will be related to larger piles of wood in schools.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O' the Pines fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good with fish holding on timber in 15–20 feet of water. Black crappie in particular may reposition toward cleaner water as conditions settle. The fall pattern is running a little late this year, but it is beginning to take shape, and crappie action should steadily improve on the south end of the lake. Crappie are moving down the lake towards the dam. Crappie are fair with hair jigs while fish holding on structure in the main channel and on structure on the flats right off the channel.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake LBJ fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair in 20 feet of water on brush piles with minnows. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service. Look for bass suspended around grass or isolated structure and throw an Alabama rig, underspin or minnow.
reports.by: Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Limestone fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are in 8-20 feet of water on minnows. Largemouth bass are in 4-12 feet of water on brush, docks and bulkheads hitting Texas rigs and spinnerbaits.
reports.by: Colan Gonzales, Lake Limestone Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Livingston fishing report
reports.text: White bass are scattered but schooling at times on main-lake points and sandbars, hitting slabs and small spoons when active. Crappie action is improving around brush and timber in 12-20 feet, with minnows producing best. Largemouth bass are fair, with a few fish pushing shallow around wood and reeds; spinnerbaits, chatterbaits, and squarebills have been the most reliable.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Marble Falls fishing report
reports.text: Bass are feeding on shad to bulk up for the winter.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Martin Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair along the hydrilla with larger fish in deeper wood and brush piles. Crappie are fair to good with minnows, pintail jigs and small silver spoons. Tail spinners and small slab spoons work well.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Meredith fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass, smallmouth bass and sand bass all have continued to flourish around many parts of the lake. Crappie are fair at Sanford Yake Dock, North Canyon, and Fritch Fortress with pearl white, pearl blue, grey or yellow jigs and minnows.
reports.by: Dave Wright, Wright-On Bait, Tackle and Watercraft Rental

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Murvaul fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are fair with a small chartreuse squarebill crankbait or bladed jig on shallow rocky points. Crappie are excellent on standing timber with a 1/32 ounce white and chartreuse crappie jigs.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal's ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nacogdoches fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are good on Carolina rigs or deep diving crankbaits on creek channel swings. Crappie are good with black and chartreuse crappie jigs. There are a lot of bass grouping up around small depressions in the grass in 5-7 feet of water chasing bait. Bass can be caught shallow on squarebill crankbaits or chatterbaits, or in deeper water with Carolina rigged jigs or Alabama rigs.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal's ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Naconiche fishing report
reports.text: Crappie population is good, while catfish remain slow. Crappie are fair on chartreuse and black crappie jigs. Largemouth bass are fair on Carolina rigs or dropshots on main lake grassy points.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal's ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nasworthy fishing report
reports.text: The bass are heavily related to baitfish this time of year, so a good rule of thumb is find the bait and then you will find the bass. Bass are fair flipping soft plastics around reed bases in 1-5 feet of water. The key is to cover water until you find a good stretch that holds multiple bass. Bass are holding back in the shade around heavy cover to escape the sunlight. Early morning and late evening topwater is also effective for targeting bass. Baitfish are beginning to transition into the backs of pockets and upriver with the bass close behind. Crappie are fair around main lake boat docks on chartreuse jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Navarro Mills fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 12 feet brush piles with minnows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palo Pinto fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in deep water with minnows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Pinkston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are fair on flukes and bladed jigs on shallow grassy points. Crappie are good with small white pearl jigs.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal's ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Possum Kingdom fishing report
reports.text: Silver and white slab jigs have been the magic ticket. The largemouth bass winter pattern is starting. Bass are feeding on the shad around docks and structure. Bass are eating, but not in a hurry. Sand bass are good in 20-30 feet of water on main lake points and sand flats with white slabs.
reports.by: Captain Casey Armstrong, Hooked Up Outfitters

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Proctor fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are on ledges in about 15-18 feet. Bass are moving to deep ledges.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Raven fishing report
reports.text: No catches have been reported this week, and it is likely that largemouth bass have moved deeper water seeking more stable temperatures, becoming less aggressive in their feeding. Anglers targeting bass should focus on deeper structures like submerged logs or drop-offs near creek channels. The fishing piers continue to see steady activity, for anglers targeting crappie and bluegill.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Roberts fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are fair to good running in pockets, ditches and draws with a swim jig. Crappie are good with natural colored jigs or minnows. Sand bass are fair on humps with live bait, or slabs. Dan's Crappie Co.
reports.by: Daniel Koberna, Lt. Dan's Crappie Co

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Richland Chambers fishing report
reports.text: Idle these main lake areas until you locate fish then drop a 2 ounce slab with a bucktail jig or spoon 18 inches above the slab. Black bass can be caught on shallow cover following schools of shad. Target larger bass with a swimbait or glide bait.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Sam Rayburn fishing report
reports.text: Bass are pushing shallow and chasing shad with the influx of new water, and any remaining grass in holding fish. Everything is on the move upriver or into shallow zones with the rising water, and both crappie and white bass are also making their way upriver. The major populations of bass are in 10-15 feet of water or 20-25 feet of water on main lake drains, or secondary points and creek channel swings.
reports.by: Captain Lynn Atkinson, Reel Um N Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Somerville fishing report
reports.text: On the lake crappie are fair with various jigs and minnows holding tight to brush in 8-12 feet of water. Black bass are fair on craw jigs and slow plastic baits in 6-14 feet of water.
reports.by: Weldon Kirk, Fish Tales Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stamford fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good with crankbaits and spinnerbaits on points and shallow in 3-5 feet of water. Crappie are good with pink and white or black and chartreuse jigs in 9-11 feet of water on brush or concrete structures. Some crappie can be caught in the crappie house.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tawakoni fishing report
reports.text: Best depths have been 10-20 feet with swimbaits and slabs. Crappie have improved in 10-18 feet of water on bridge pilings, docks and vertical timber are holding fish. Largemouth bass are good on squarebill crankbaits in super shallow water next to dock legs and shallow stickups.
reports.by: Captain Michael Littlejohn, Lake Tawakoni Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texana fishing report
reports.text: Bass action is hit-or-miss, but anglers are finding fish shallow around wood and vegetation, with spinnerbaits, chatterbaits, and soft plastics producing the best results. Crappie reports continue to improve, with anglers picking up fish on brush in 10-18 feet using minnows and small jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texoma fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are in brush and structure in 8-12 feet of water with fish being suspended near the top of the water column. Stripers are good in 10-30 feet of water in ditches, drop-offs and ledges near flats with slabs, live bait, and Alabama rigs.
reports.by: Jacob Orr, Lake Texoma, Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Toledo Bend fishing report
reports.text: Anglers are still catching good numbers of bass, but fewer quality fish have been reported.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Travis fishing report
reports.text: Before the front bass were good on small topwaters at the marinas. Bass were good on bluff walls 30-35 feet down bouncing a football head jig with a craw on it on the ledges.
reports.by: Randal Frisbee, Central Texas Fishing Guide, LLC

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Waco fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow to fair in 12-18 feet of water in standing timber, brush piles and other structures. Crappie are not very active so you will have to work for a bite. Report by Greg Culverhouse, Crappie King.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Whitney fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair in the main lake brush in 20-30 feet of water. White bass are slow on slabs in 20 feet of water. Largemouth bass are fair using soft plastics on deep structure and around docks.
reports.by: Captain Cory Vinson, Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Worth fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing is good along cattails and under concrete bridge pilings using crankbaits with big vibration. Crappie are slow. Sand bass are good in deeper water on slabs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Wright Patman fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair on hair jigs while fish are scattered at all depths.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Amistad fishing report
reports.text: Weather conditions at the lake this past week have been warm with light winds, and bass patterns have stayed consistent. Another cooling trend in the forecast should help increase bass activity. Crappie fishing has been good for several weeks on small jigs and plastic tubes, and a few anglers have also found success catching catfish in the Pecos River. Report by Kurt Dove, Amistad Bass Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Arlington fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth and sand bass can be caught on a variety of imitation shad lures. Crappie are in schools in brush piles around main creek channels and ditches.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Athens fishing report
reports.text: Bass are feeding on shad and bluegill gearing up for winter. Bass can be caught on weightless 5 inch stick bait or 5 inch soft jerkbait in shad and bluegill patterns. Crappie are schooled up on main lake brush piles hitting crappie jigs or minnows.
reports.by: Captain Kirk Pasalich, Artifishable Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Austin fishing report
reports.text: The bass bite is slowing.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bob Sandlin fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in river channels to the highway 21 bridge and in secondary depressions on timber in 20-40 feet of water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bois d'Arc fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good in the morning and mid morning on chatterbaits and spinnerbaits around grass and wind blown points or flats 2-4 feet. Bass are good with Texas rigs and jigs on big trees just off the edge of Timber Creek, and in 6-7 feet with creature baits or beavers. Crappie are good on minnows or jigs midlake in the river channel from the 897 bridge to the dam. Targeting crappie can be tough on windy days.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Braunig fishing report
reports.text: Redfish, stripers, and black bass are all sluggish with limited activity.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brownwood fishing report
reports.text: Black bass to 4.25 pounds are good in 13-28 feet of water in the river with soft plastic minnow styled baits and juice box colored soft plastic creature bait. Crappie up to 14 inches are good on minnows and jigs in main lake scattered brush piles in 8-18 feet. White bass up to 1.25 pounds are slow on crappie jigs and crankbaits in the lights at night.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bryan fishing report
reports.text: Bass bite is slow and inconsistent for most of the day, but starts to pick up in the late afternoon once the fish become more active.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Caddo fishing report
reports.text: Some bass can be caught on flukes, frogs and punching grass mats mixed up in the lily pads.
reports.by: Vince Richards, Caddo Lake Fishing & Fellowship

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Calaveras fishing report
reports.text: Black bass action is slow, and stripers are also sluggish.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Canyon Lake fishing report
reports.text: Water temperatures are ranging from the high 30s one week and 70s the next so the bass are scattered.
reports.by: Tyler Stanley, Game on Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Choke Canyon fishing report
reports.text: White bass, black bass, and crappie remain slow.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Coleto Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing is fair at best, with most action coming around timber in 3-8 feet of water.
reports.by: Scott Springer, Fish Choke Canyon Lake

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Comanche Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are good on crankbaits and soft plastics.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Conroe fishing report
reports.text: Bass have been good along banks, grasslands, and docks throughout the day, with a few coming offshore structure around midday; Texas-rigged creature baits are working well. Crappie continue to produce solid numbers and a mix of quality fish and juveniles, with minnows performing best on structure in 12-21 feet and hair jigs close behind. Hybrids are scattered and schooling on flats in 14-23 feet, hitting slabs, spoons, and shad, with mostly smaller schools but some larger groups mixed in.
reports.by: Brad Doyle with Bradley’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Dunlap fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good with many limits reported. Early morning bass are biting on buzzbaits, then later in the afternoon switch to soft plastics, or crawfish colored crankbaits under the docks in 8 feet of water. Crappie are good in 10-15 feet of water in the trees with minnows.
reports.by: Lee Johnson and Kenneth Linder, local anglers

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fayette fishing report
reports.text: Bass can be targeted in shallow water rattle traps or spinnerbaits or in 12-15 feet of water on shaky heads, dropshot or Carolina rigs. or on shaky heads in deeper water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fork fishing report
reports.text: There is a good shallow bass bite. around grass on chatterbaits, spinnerbaits and some topwaters. Black Bass are feeding in the backs of creeks and coves. Cooler nights have dropped water temperatures and bass are cruising the shallows. Streamers are enticing bass early and late in the day. Crappie are good as the fish transition to a fall and winter pattern. Small hand tied jigs actually out fished minnows this week on my boat but any crappie baits will get you bit as water temps cool down.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ft. Phantom Hill fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on structure with minnows or jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granbury fishing report
reports.text: Sand bass are fair to good mid-lake on slabs and spinnerbaits. Crappie action continues to be good on small jigs and minnows fished on standing structure mid lake. Largemouth bass are schooling early with the sand bass and small striped bass. Some good reports for largemouth bass in the river north of Granbury near laydowns with spinnerbaits and crankbaits early, then soft plastics later in the day.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granger fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are slow. Crappie are fair on jigs fished in standing timber.
reports.by: Tommy Tidwell, Tommy Tidwell's Granger Lake Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Grapevine fishing report
reports.text: Target sand bass in 12-15 feet of water near drop-offs with smaller imitation shad slabs fished off the bottom. Use white slabs if the water clarity becomes stained. Bass and catfish are mixed in with the sandies.
reports.by: Omar Cotter, Luck O'the Irish Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Hawkins fishing report
reports.text: Small poppers fished around grass and isolated stumps should draw a strike from black bass.
reports.by: Guide Alex Guthrie, Fly Fish Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are snapping from midlake to the south end, as well as in pockets of the East Fork and West Fork, hitting spinnerbaits, chatterbaits, crankbaits, Texas-rigged worms and grubs, and even some early topwater if you time it right; points, second drop-offs, and nearby docks are producing best. Crappie are strong in Luces Bayou and the East Fork, tight to structure and biting minnows and small jigs, especially during low-pressure periods. White bass are active on the south end with good size, caught trolling jet divers with #12 pet spoons, vertical jigging half-ounce slabs, or working deep-diving crankbaits over humps.
reports.by: Captain Zackary Scott, Zack Attack Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Jacksonville fishing report
reports.text: Bass are tough with a few bites on jigs and soft plastics around docks, brush, and points.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O' the Pines fishing report
reports.text: Bass can still be caught in 3-5 feet of water around major creek channels using Texas Rigged creature baits and squarebill crankbaits. Crappie can be found suspended around standing timber in 20-22 feet of water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lewisville fishing report
reports.text: Hybrid striper and white bass are slow on points and humps in 10-30 feet of water with slabs, spoons, spinnerbaits, and swimbaits. Crappie are fair in 10-34 feet of water on brush piles, submerged timber, laydowns, and rock piles. More crappie have been showing up around the bridge pilings as well.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Livingston fishing report
reports.text: White bass are scattered but showing up in small schools on mid-lake humps, taking slabs and small spoons when you can stay on them. Black bass are fair, with the best action coming early around bulkheads, grass lines, and shallow rocky points on spinnerbaits, crankbaits, and Texas-rigged worms; a few fish are showing up midday on deeper brush. Crappie are fair around docks and timber in 10-18 feet, with minnows producing slightly better than jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Martin Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair fishing the hydrilla with senkos and flukes. Larger bass are around offshore brush and clay points in 10-25 feet using Carolina rig worms and black-blue jigs with trailers. Crappie are fair with one or two fish being caught per tree in standing timber in 20-25 feet of water with pintail jigs and minnows. Sand bass are good on small slab spoons at the county line road bridge and Dirgin bridge in 20-25 feet.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Meredith fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass and sand bass are great with suspended jerkbaits in north canyon, as well as chartreuse chatter baits along the banks before Bugbee. Crappie are fair in Sanford Yake Dock, North Canyon, and Fritch Fortress.
reports.by: Dave Wright, Wright-On Bait, Tackle and Watercraft Rental

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Naconiche fishing report
reports.text: Crappie populations remain good, while catfish continue to be slow. Largemouth are slow rattle traps and bladed jigs on shallow grass lines. Crappie are slow to fair with chartreuse jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nasworthy fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair flipping soft plastics around reed bases in 1-5 feet of water. The key is to cover water until you find a good stretch that holds multiple bass. Bass are holding back in the shade around heavy cover to escape the sunlight. Early morning and late evening topwater is also effective for targeting bass. Baitfish are beginning to transition into the backs of pockets and upriver with the bass close behind. Crappie are fair around main lake boat docks on chartreuse jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O.H. Ivie fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are good for 5 pound fish. Good numbers of schooling bass throughout the lake. Target bass in the pockets and drains with 3 inch shad patterned swimbaits on quarter ounce heads. Very few reports of crappie limits. Target crappie in the Turkey Bend area suspended down 18-25 feet on main lake pecan trees in 30-25 feet of water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palo Pinto fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are on deep water brush piles biting minnows. Black bass, sand bass and hybrids are slow.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Proctor fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are on the rocks near the dam.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Richland Chambers fishing report
reports.text: Black bass can be caught on brush piles. This time of year you can spot wolf packs of bass chasing large shad in shallow water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Somerville fishing report
reports.text: At the marina crappie are fair. On the lake crappie are fair with various jigs and minnows holding tight to brush in 6-12 feet of water. Black bass are fair on craw jigs and slow plastic baits in 6-14 feet of water.
reports.by: Weldon Kirk, Fish Tales Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tawakoni fishing report
reports.text: Slabs and swimbaits are working best in 5-10 feet. Crappie are good on jigs and minnows under bridges and on timber in 12-16 feet. Largemouth bass are good in 1-4 feet of water on dock legs and riprap with shallow crankbaits, shaky heads and spinnerbaits.
reports.by: Captain Michael Littlejohn, Lake Tawakoni Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texoma fishing report
reports.text: Look for bigger crappie roaming 8-12 feet on stump flats and in the backs of coves. Stripers are good on the ledges and dropshots in 15-30 feet of water on drop-offs and ledges with slabs.
reports.by: Jacob Orr, Lake Texoma, Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Travis fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good on small topwaters at the marinas for 2-3 pound fish. Bass are good on bluff walls 30-35 feet down bouncing a football head jig with a craw on it on the ledges.
reports.by: Randal Frisbee, Central Texas Fishing Guide, LLC

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Twin Buttes fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair scattered in 14-18 feet of water on brush piles.
reports.by: Captain Michael Peterson, 4 Reel Fun Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Waco fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair in 12-18 feet of water in standing timber, brush piles and other structures. Report by Greg Culverhouse, Crappie King.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Weatherford fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow around docks with crankbaits. Crappie are fair on brush piles with minnows and jigs. Crappie are showing up in the crappie house.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Whitney fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are in the main lake brush in 20-30 feet of water. White bass are fair on slabs in 20 feet of water. Largemouth bass are fair using soft plastics on deep structure and around docks.
reports.by: Captain Cory Vinson, Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Worth fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good on rocky and gravel banks using crankbaits with vibration thrown up against the cattails. Crappie are slow. Sand bass are excellent on slabs and trolling crankbaits in the main lake.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Wright Patman fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are biting crappie jigs on the flats off the river channel and are currently holding on structure.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Alan Henry fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 25-35 feet over trees with minnows.
reports.by: Randy Britton, The Bait Shop, Post, Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Arlington fishing report
reports.text: Many bass are still in shallow water, but focus on the areas near deep water for a more consistent bite. Crappie are schooled up in deep water on brush piles, with bigger crappie suspended in isolation across the basin.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Austin fishing report
reports.text: Bass are biting spinnerbaits and jerkbaits fished around main lake submerged vegetation. Bass fishing is good right now on Lake Austin.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bois d'Arc fishing report
reports.text: Morning bass bite has slowed due to the dropping water temperature. Crappie are good in the channels in 25-40 feet of water with plastic jigs over hand ties. Finding keeper size crappie can be a challenge.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Braunig fishing report
reports.text: Water stained; 69 degrees; Fishing has been slow across the board this week, with redfish, catfish, striper, and black bass all showing limited activity.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bridgeport fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 10-25 feet of water on docks, and offshore brush piles with minnows or jigs. Largemouth bass are good using topwaters on banks in the morning or for deeper schooling fish. White bass and hybrids are fair on main lake humps and points with topwaters, slabs or trolling with deep crankbaits. Report by Jack Pellegrini, Lake Bridgeport Crappie Guide Service.
reports.by: Jack Pellegrini, Lake Bridgeport Crappie Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brownwood fishing report
reports.text: Black bass to 9.25 pounds are excellent in 13-28 feet of water on imitation minnows, craws in juicebox in the rivers, and green pumpkin tornado worms in the shoreline grass. Crappie are good with catches up to 14 inches on minnows and jigs on main lake scattered brush piles in 8-18 feet. White bass are slow to 1.25 pounds on crappie jigs and crankbaits out of the lights at night.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Caddo fishing report
reports.text: Schooling black bass can be caught on chrome rattle traps, shad color chatterbaits, spinning baits and swimbaits. White bass and black bass will be good in the river very soon with Alabama rigs, rooster tails and underspins.
reports.by: Vince Richards, Caddo Lake Fishing & Fellowship

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Calaveras fishing report
reports.text: Striper and black bass action remain slow overall.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Canyon Lake fishing report
reports.text: There is good early morning schooling bass action around main lake wind blown points and banks.
reports.by: Tyler Stanley, Game on Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Cedar Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Good stacks of hybrid striped bass and white bass are being found on mid-lake points and drop-offs along sandy flats throughout the dam area, Crappie Island, Key Ranch, and the spillway humps in 12–22 feet of water. Cast spinnerbaits and slabs, and watch for schooling fish on these flats as well as around deeper seawalls and shorelines. To catch hybrids use spinnerbaits or work a slab vertically with a fast up-and-down motion for immediate strikes. A slow retrieve with a slab cast and reeled steadily back is also effective. Try rattle traps, spoons, umbrella rigs, slabs, or sassy shads to trigger bites. The crappie bite continues to improve. Target crappie with small jigs and minnows in…
reports.by: Brent Herbeck, Herbeck’s Lonestar Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Choke Canyon fishing report
reports.text: Bank fishing, however, is excellent right now, with good catches of channel and blue catfish, crappie, black bass, and white bass all being reported from the shoreline.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Coleto Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing is fair, with most catches coming from timber in 5-10 feet of water using soft plastics.
reports.by: Scott Springer, Fish Choke Canyon Lake

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Comanche Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass numbers are excellent on soft plastics and crankbaits. Some anglers are reporting catches around 100 bass per day with some bigger fish to 6 pounds possible.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Conroe fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are active, biting crankbaits on shad–loaded, wind-blown points, moving offshore during the day, and along banks and grasslines early and late. Crappie catches are improving, with anglers finding better numbers - though many are still small - around timber and structure in 12-21 feet using minnows, hair jigs, or plastics. Hybrids remain scattered and schooling, taking slabs, spoons, or shad off flats and drop-off edges in 16-23 feet, with a mix of smaller pods and a few larger schools.
reports.by: Brad Doyle with Bradley’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Eagle Mountain fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on jigs and minnows around boat docks. Black bass are fair around boat docks on swim baits and jerkbaits. Sand bass are fair on slabs on main lake humps.
reports.by: Captain Bobby Mann, Catch a Dream Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Falcon fishing report
reports.text: Reports are saying the crappie fishing has been great and catfishing is steady as usual for this time of year. Crappie are being caught on isolated brush piles and standing timber in about 20 feet of water using artificial lures.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fayette fishing report
reports.text: A few bass can be caught on shallow points with rattle traps, or on shaky heads in deeper water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fork fishing report
reports.text: The morning bass bite has slowed due to cool fronts and dropping water temperatures. Black Bass are beginning to school in open water. Cooler nights have dropped water temperatures and bass are cruising. Streamers are enticing bass early and late. Crappie are good as the fish transition to a fall and winter pattern. Small hand tied jigs actually out fished minnows this week on my boat but any crappie baits will get you bit as water temps cool down.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ft. Phantom Hill fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on structure with jigs and minnows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granbury fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are good in numbers with an occasional bigger fish. Crappie action continues to be good to excellent on small minnows and jigs fished on submerged structure. The best crappie action is from near Indian Harbor to Bent water on submerged timber and near bridge pilings.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granger fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are fair up the river and around main lake structures with worms and crankbaits. Crappie are fair on jigs fished in standing timber.
reports.by: Tommy Tidwell, Tommy Tidwell's Granger Lake Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Grapevine fishing report
reports.text: White bass are feeding heavily with mixed bags of crappie and catfish mixed in. Water clarity has improved, so use Irish special or shad slabs fished off the bottom.
reports.by: Omar Cotter, Luck O'the Irish Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are active around docks and shallow cover, especially early in the morning near riprap, brush, and shallow dock ends, hitting well on spinnerbaits, crankbaits, and Texas-rigged worms before moving slightly deeper later in the day. Crappie are holding tight to structure in the East Fork and Lucious Bayou, biting live minnows and hand-tied jigs in silver, chartreuse, or darker colors when the water muddies.
reports.by: Captain Zackary Scott, Zack Attack Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Jacksonville fishing report
reports.text: Bass are keying on shad all over the lake.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O' the Pines fishing report
reports.text: Prior to the cold snap, bass were being caught in 3–5 feet of water on 1.5 square-bill crankbaits and bladed jigs. With the arrival of the cold front, crappie have pushed a few feet deeper in the water column, with the best bite coming from 14–18 feet.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake LBJ fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair in 20 feet of water on brush piles with minnows. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service.
reports.by: Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Limestone fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are in 8-20 feet on minnows. Largemouth bass are in 4-12 feet of water on brush, docks and bulkheads hitting Texas rigs and spinnerbaits.
reports.by: Colan Gonzales, Lake Limestone Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Livingston fishing report
reports.text: White bass are schooling on main lake points and humps, chasing shad and hitting slabs and small spoons. Crappie are fair around brush piles and standing timber in 12-18 feet of water on minnows and jigs. Largemouth bass are fair on crankbaits and Texas rigs worked along rocky points and submerged timber, especially early and late in the day.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Martin Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good with flukes, senkos and lipless crankbaits over the hydrilla. Crappie are fair using pintail jigs and minnows. Crappie are scattered in the timber in 20-25 feet of water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Murvaul fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are slow on shallow diving crankbaits and bladed jigs. Crappie are excellent on standing timber with chartreuse and black crappie jigs. Catfish are good with cut bait, live minnows, or crappie jigs.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal's ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nacogdoches fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are excellent on swimbaits along grass lines, and bladed jigs in shallow water. Crappie are fair in standing timber with live minnows or chartreuse jigs.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal's ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Naconiche fishing report
reports.text: Crappie action remains solid, while catfish have been slow. Largemouth are slow rattle traps and bladed jigs on shallow grass lines. Crappie are slow to fair with chartreuse jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O.H. Ivie fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are good in creeks and pockets feeding on shad. Crappie are fair with scattered limits reported on minnows around deep brush and trees.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palo Pinto fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are biting chartreuse and gray jigs or blackjigs. Black bass are slow.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Pinkston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are fair for fish between 3-6 pounds. Crappie are fair on brush piles. Bluegill are excellent on small crappie jigs with a slip bobber.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal's ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Possum Kingdom fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on docks and brush. Bass are fair on swimbaits and crankbaits. Sand bass are really starting to stack up on points on the north end of the lake, and slabs bounced off the bottom will produce solid numbers. Sand bass are good in 15-30 feet of water on main lake points and sand flats with chrome and white slabs.
reports.by: Captain Casey Armstrong, Hooked Up Outfitters

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Hubbard fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good, and also moving.
reports.by: John Varner, John Varner's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Roberts fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good off creek channels in 12-18 feet of water with green and chartreuse jigs. Largemouth bass are good with buzz baits and topwater lures. Sand bass are fair on humps with live bait, or slabs. Dan's Crappie Co.
reports.by: Daniel Koberna, Lt. Dan's Crappie Co

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Richland Chambers fishing report
reports.text: White bass are being caught on slabs and in-line spinners on points and humps in 18-25 feet. Black bass are going to start following the shad to the creek channels in the main lake coves.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Somerville fishing report
reports.text: At the marina crappie are slow. On the lake crappie are fair with various jigs and minnows over brush in 6-12 feet of water. Black bass are fair on craw jigs and slow plastic baits in 6-14 feet of water.
reports.by: Weldon Kirk, Fish Tales Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stillhouse fishing report
reports.text: Fall conditions have bass scattered, making it difficult to find big groups or consistent patterns. Large schools of nomadic bass are roaming the main lake chasing shad. Bass fishing is fair utilizing forward-facing sonar and mid-strolling small minnow-style soft plastics.
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texoma fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are moving on structure and docks. Brush is loaded with smaller fish and bigger crappie will move in as water temps cool. Target the flats in less than 30 feet of water slabs, live bait, and some swimbaits.
reports.by: Jacob Orr, Lake Texoma, Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Toledo Bend fishing report
reports.text: Water temperatures have finally cooled into the mid-60s, putting bass on the feed.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Travis fishing report
reports.text: Cooling fall weather has improved the bass bite, though conditions remain variable. Focus on transition areas with a mix of brush and rock for quality largemouth. Forward-facing sonar can be used to locate schools of bass roaming open water following baitfish, with suspending jerkbaits producing steady action. Bass are very good targeting fish shallow around rocky points and brush near the mouths of coves.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Twin Buttes fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are in 14-18 feet of water on brush piles.
reports.by: Captain Michael Peterson, 4 Reel Fun Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tyler fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on minnows or jigs 10-20 feet of water on brush piles. Bass are fair on trick worms and crankbaits.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: White River fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair on brush piles with jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Whitney fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are in the main lake brush in 20-30 feet of water. Largemouth bass are good using soft plastics on deep structure and around docks.
reports.by: Captain Cory Vinson, Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Worth fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good using chatterbaits in shallow water and on rocky banks. Crappie are slow. Sand bass being caught on the deeper end of the lake, bumping slabs off of the bottom.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Amistad fishing report
reports.text: Water temperatures have finally dropped into the 70s, and the recent South Texas cold front has pushed bait and bass toward the backs of pockets. Buzzbaits and other topwater lures are producing well during low-light conditions, while some bass are relating to new grass growth from the recent rise in water levels. Report by Kurt Dove, Amistad Bass Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Aquilla fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on brush piles in 20-25 feet of water with minnows and jigs. Bass are good on spinnerbaits in 5-10 feet of water.
reports.by: Captain Cory Vinson, Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Arlington fishing report
reports.text: Focus on these low spots around flats to find game fish like largemouth, white bass, catfish and crappie.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Benbrook fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair next to timber in 15-30 feet on minnows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bob Sandlin fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are excellent in river channels to the highway 21 bridge and in secondary depressions on timber in 20-40 feet of water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bois d'Arc fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good in 2-5 feet of water on points or grass early in the day with choppos, topwater frogs, and rage swimmers. Crappie are good in the channels in 25-40 feet of water with plastic jigs over hand ties. Finding keeper size crappie can be a challenge.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Braunig fishing report
reports.text: Stripers and black bass are also sluggish, showing little activity.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bridgeport fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 10-25 feet on docks, and offshore brush piles, minnows are best but the jig bite is good. Largemouth bass are good using topwaters for deeper schooling fish or on banks in the morning, flukes, senkos, and chatterbaits on main lake rock and docks. White bass and hybrids are biting good on main lake humps and points with topwaters, slabs or trolling. Report by Jack Pellegrini, Lake Bridgeport Crappie Guide Service.
reports.by: Jack Pellegrini, Lake Bridgeport Crappie Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brownwood fishing report
reports.text: Black bass to 5.96 pounds are excellent in 3-8 feet of water on Hag’s Cheat codes in juice box in the rivers, or with green pumpkin tornados in shoreline grass. Crappie are excellent with minnows and jigs scattered on main lake brush piles in 12-20 feet of water. White bass are slow, 1.50 pounds fish, on crappie jigs and crankbaits out of the lights at night.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Caddo fishing report
reports.text: The bass had a locked jaw, but would hit a shad colored rattle trap or chatterbait. The crappie bite improves this time of year, as long the clarity does not get too muddy.
reports.by: Vince Richards, Caddo Lake Fishing & Fellowship

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Calaveras fishing report
reports.text: Black bass and stripers are also slow this week, showing limited activity overall.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Canyon Lake fishing report
reports.text: The bass fishing is picking up!
reports.by: Tyler Stanley, Game on Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Choke Canyon fishing report
reports.text: White bass are slow while crappie and gaspergou are fair.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Comanche Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Comanche Creek continues to boast excellent numbers for largemouth bass up to 6 pounds. Bass are being caught on crankbaits, soft plastics and spinnerbaits.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Conroe fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are active up shallow, hitting rattle traps and creature baits. Crappie numbers are improving, with fish holding on various structures in 12-21 feet and biting on minnows, hair jigs, and plastics - hair jigs and minnows have been especially productive. Hybrid stripers are scattered and schooling in smaller groups, found on flats and drop-off edges in 12-22 feet, and biting on slabs, spoons, and shad.
reports.by: Brad Doyle with Bradley’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cooper fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are in the river channels migrating to the dam.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cypress Springs fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are excellent in the old river channels dropping jigs down and shaking them.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Eagle Mountain fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on jigs and minnows around boat dock and over deep water brush piles. Black bass are good on swimbaits and spinnerbaits in 4-6 feet of water.
reports.by: Captain Bobby Mann, Catch a Dream Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fayette fishing report
reports.text: When you find bass the same techniques should work.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fork fishing report
reports.text: Early morning bass bite is good but did slow down after the cold front. Black Bass are beginning to school in open water. Cooler nights have dropped water temperatures and bass are cruising. Streamers are enticing bass early and late. Crappie are good as the fish transition to a fall and winter pattern. Small hand tied jigs actually out fished minnows this week on my boat but any crappie baits will get you bit as water temps cool down.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ft. Phantom Hill fishing report
reports.text: Crappie fair on minnows and jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Graham fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on brush in 13-15 feet with minnows. The bass bite is good with topwater baits as in the back of pockets while bass feed on shad.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granbury fishing report
reports.text: Sand bass continue to be good mid-lake on slabs fished in 10-15 feet of water. Largemouth bass are good in numbers near major creek entrances. Some of the largemouth are schooling with the sand bass. Crappie action continues to be good to excellent on small jigs and minnows fished on submerged timber and bridge pilings and deeper docks.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granger fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are fair on worms and crankbaits fished in shallow cover. Crappie are fair on jigs fished in timber from 6-13 feet deep.
reports.by: Tommy Tidwell, Tommy Tidwell's Granger Lake Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Grapevine fishing report
reports.text: Water clarity is stained due to the high winds last week, so use white slabs and scented slabs to help entice the bite. Continue to look for working birds and target fish jigging slabs in 15-17 feet of water.
reports.by: Omar Cotter, Luck O'the Irish Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Hawkins fishing report
reports.text: There is an early and late bite on small topwater patterns for bass and bream. Watch for schooling bass mid-lake.
reports.by: Guide Alex Guthrie, Fly Fish Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are active in the shallows, hitting chatterbaits, spinnerbaits, and small green grubs, with Texas-rigged setups working well around boat docks and riprap. Crappie fishing is excellent in 8-14 feet of water near structure, biting well on minnows and silver hand-tied jigs. White bass are stacked up on humps in 12-14 feet on the south end, hitting slabs, rattle traps, and deep-diving crankbaits, with #12 pet spoons tipped with gold feathers producing steady action.
reports.by: Captain Zackary Scott, Zack Attack Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O' the Pines fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in timber off main channels in 18-24 feet of water with 2 inch plastics. Crappie fishing has been productive as fish push deeper with the cooling trend. White crappie are holding in mid-lake timber 10–12 feet down, a little spooky but willing to bite once you settle in. Black crappie are balled up tight on standing timber 12–18 feet deep, with the best action coming off laydowns and angled timber, which continue to out-fish straight-pole trees. Bass are being caught in brush piles 12–14 feet deep on jigs and Texas-rigged creature baits.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lavon fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are great in 15-20 feet on structure with igs and minnows. Some black bass are in 2-10 feet of water. A few bass have been caught on a ledge in 22 feet, but the best catches are in 10-15 feet when the sun comes up with a squarebill crankbait and 12 foot series 5 diver, watermelon red watermelon green creature baits, or plastic worms.
reports.by: Carey Thorn, White Bass Fishing Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake LBJ fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair in 15-20 feet of water on brush piles with minnows. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service.
reports.by: Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lewisville fishing report
reports.text: Slabs, spoons, spinnerbaits and live bait are working. Crappie are fair in 10-34 feet of water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Livingston fishing report
reports.text: White bass are beginning to school up on main-lake points and humps, hitting slabs and small spoons. Largemouth bass are fair, with fish moving shallow in the mornings to feed on shad - try spinnerbaits, chatterbaits, or square-bill crankbaits near grass lines and docks. Crappie are fair to good around bridge pilings and submerged brush in 12-18 feet, using minnows or small jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Martin Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good along the hydrilla with senkos, swimbaits and lipless crankbaits. Crappie are fair to good around timber in 20-25 feet with minnows and jigs. Large catfish are where the crappie are.
reports.by: Hambone Fishing Report by Hambone Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Meredith fishing report
reports.text: Smallmouth bass and sand bass are great trolling and jigging. Crappie are slow at the Sanford Yake Dock, blue west, and Bugbee.
reports.by: Dave Wright, Wright-On Bait, Tackle and Watercraft Rental

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nacogdoches fishing report
reports.text: Crappie fishing is excellent on Lake Nacogdoches, with good numbers holding on standing timber in the middle of the lake. Bass are fair on Carolina rigs and drop shots around secondary points, and also hitting flukes and spinnerbaits in shallow water near stumps.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal's ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Naconiche fishing report
reports.text: Crappie numbers are looking good, while catfish action remains slow. Largemouth are excellent on topwater frogs shallow near grass. Black crappie are excellent with small white crappie jigs over brush piles.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Navarro Mills fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are great in deep brush piles with minnows. No reports of white bass or largemouth bass.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O.H. Ivie fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are good to 8 pounds on topwater frogs and 6 inch worms in green pumpkin plum or red apple in 6-12 feet are best depth. Crappie are slowing down and moving into their winter positions.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palestine fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 16-25 feet of water with jigs or minnows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palo Pinto fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are slow. Crappie are good in deep water with minnows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Possum Kingdom fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on docks and brush. Bass are fair on swimbaits and crankbaits.
reports.by: Captain Casey Armstrong, Hooked Up Outfitters

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Raven fishing report
reports.text: No catches have been reported this week, and it’s likely that largemouth bass have moved deeper water seeking more stable temperatures, becoming less aggressive in their feeding. Anglers targeting bass should focus on deeper structures like submerged logs or drop-offs near creek channels. The fishing piers continue to see steady activity, with anglers going after crappie and bluegill - though no confirmed catches, the consistent presence of fishermen suggests some are finding success.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Richland Chambers fishing report
reports.text: White bass are good in 17-25 feet of water on slabs with a small buck tail jig 18 inches above. Black Bass are on the move as well. Bass are around docks and structure between docks.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Somerville fishing report
reports.text: At the marina crappie are slow. On the lake crappie are good with various jigs and minnows over brush in 6-12 feet of water. Black bass are fair on craw jigs and slow plastics baits in 6-14 feet of water.
reports.by: Weldon Kirk, Fish Tales Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stillhouse fishing report
reports.text: Bass are also hitting hard and soft jerkbaits in the same areas when chasing baitfish near the rocks.
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texoma fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are moving on structure and docks. Brush is loaded with smaller fish and bigger crappie will move in as water temps cool. Stripers are good with slabs in 10-30 feet of water.
reports.by: Jacob Orr, Lake Texoma, Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Travis fishing report
reports.text: Focus on transition areas with a mix of brush and rock for quality largemouth. Bass are very good targeting fish shallow around rocky points and brush near the mouths of coves.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Waco fishing report
reports.text: Crappie bite was excellent before the cold front. Report by Greg Culverhouse, Crappie King.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Whitney fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are in main lake brush in 20-30 feet of water. Largemouth bass are good using soft plastics on deep structure and around docks.
reports.by: Captain Cory Vinson, Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Worth fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good when the sun is up on points and deeper structure. Crappie are slow, but some are caught using minnows around bridge pylons. Sand bass are good on the deeper end of the lake using slabs and small crankbaits.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Wright Patman fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in timber off main channels in 18-24 feet of water with 2 inch plastics.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Amistad fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are slow on Ned rigs, shaky heads, Texas rigged senkos in watermelon red, red shad, motor oil, tequila sunrise in 15-25 feet on ledges.
reports.by: Captain Raul Cordero, Far West Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Austin fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good with worms on the edge of deep grass, then work flukes on the shallow portion of grass. Bass are feeding on smaller bait fish so cast small swimbaits and jerkbaits near mouths of creeks.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bastrop fishing report
reports.text: Moving baits around the grass beds are producing some nice bass. Targeting rock piles and ledges with shaky heads and Carolina rigs will still catch numbers of bass. Bass are good with natural colored soft plastic worms in 2-10 feet.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bois d'Arc fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow, but spinnerbaits and chatterbaits are fair in 3-6 feet around points with weeds and some shallower tree lines and road beds. Crappie fishing is excellent in the main river channel timber and lower third of the lake in 30-50 feet of water catching crappie 6-28 feet down. Fish are very healthy with big black crappie being caught on jigs.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Braunig fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair along weed lines and inside the weeds.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bridgeport fishing report
reports.text: Crappie have been slow, minnows on main lake brush piles and docks would be the best bet. Largemouth bass have been fair on small crankbaits. Hybrids and sand bass have been slow on slabs in the main lake.
reports.by: Keith Bunch, Lake Bridgeport Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brownwood fishing report
reports.text: Black bass to 5 pounds are fair on buzz baits and Hags Hurricane Bladed jigs in the grass and weeds, and with crankbaits off the rocks in 3-8 feet around the rock cuts and flats. Crappie are slow around docks in 9 feet with brush using white or black and chartreuse jigs and some offshore brush piles. White bass are slow on crankbaits and slabs scattered around the lake.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Buchanan fishing report
reports.text: Live shad has been producing some fish but slabs are out fishing the bait. Crappie are fair on brush piles and standing timber in 20-25 feet of water with minnows. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service. Lake Buchanan bass fishing is great, and the colder the better on this lake.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Caddo fishing report
reports.text: Bass are biting in the river system with crankbaits, rattle traps, chatterbaits, swimbaits and Alabama rigs. Target the cuts, turns and points in the river and to locate bass. The white bass and crappie should start up pretty soon also with the cold weather and if we keep some current.
reports.by: Vince Richards, Caddo Lake Fishing & Fellowship

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Calaveras fishing report
reports.text: Some bass are being caught off the dam and weed lines on plastics.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Cedar Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Still finding hybrids and white bass on midlake points and drop offs along sandy flats throughout the dam area, Crappie Island, Key Ranch and the spillway humps in 11-19 feet. Cast spinners and slabs and look for schooling fish on these flats as well as deeper seawalls and shorelines. Use spinnerbaits or drop a slab down to the bottom and work it fast up and down and the fish will hit it immediately. Also throwing out a slab and reeling it back with a slow retrieve is also working well. Cast rattle traps, Spoons, Umbrella Rigs, slabs or sassy shads to get the hybrids to bite. The crappie bite has been getting better. Target crappie with small jigs and minnows in 7-15 feet under bridge…
reports.by: Brent Herbeck, Herbeck’s Lonestar Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Comanche Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Comanche Creek stays warmer due to the power plant and this attracts many bass anglers in the winter.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Conroe fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good along the bank and in 30 feet of water chasing schooling shad. Crappie are fair and you will need to hit many spots to catch a limit. Many folks are trolling with a deep diver and a pet spoon trailer, others are using slabs from Bradley Outdoors to jig for them, as well as casting swimbaits or crankbaits when schooled up.
reports.by: Brad Doyle with Bradley’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fayette fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good but can be a challenge to locate after the turnover, so utilize electronics to locate fish.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fork fishing report
reports.text: Bass morning bite has been slow with a few coming on spinnerbaits and chatterbaits in 3-5 feet around grass and flats. Black bass are sporadic around vegetation. The crappie fishing on Lake Fork is heating up as the water temperature cools to the lower 60s. The crappie are following the bait fish and beginning to stack up in those areas on timber and brush. The big white crappie are in the middle sections of the timber. You can still find groups of black crappie in different depths. Some black crappie are grouped up at the base of trees in 13-18 feet close to deep water areas.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Georgetown fishing report
reports.text: Bass are best in the morning and evening on soft plastics.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granbury fishing report
