reports.text: Slabs and spinnerbaits are your best bet for these tasty sand bass from the lower ends all the way to Tin Top. Largemouth bass are good in numbers in the same areas as the sand bass. The bigger largemouths are being caught on Texas rigged soft plastics near main lake points. Crappie are located near submerged structures from Water’s Edge to the Peninsula and are good on small minnows and jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granger fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are slow. Crappie are slow on jigs fished along drop offs along the river channel.
reports.by: Tommy Tidwell, Tommy Tidwell’s Granger Lake Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Grapevine fishing report
reports.text: White bass are shallow 15-20 feet along the edges of points with white slabs.
reports.by: Omar Cotter, Luck O’the Irish Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are on cypress trees and structures in 4-5 feet biting worms and grubs. Crappie are decent on brush piles in 8-14 feet of water with hand tied jig heads in East fork.
reports.by: Captain Zackary Scott, Zack Attack Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston County fishing report
reports.text: Crappie can be caught on brush with minnows and jigs. Bass can be caught on small swimbaits.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Joe Pool Lake fishing report
reports.text: Small bass can be caught on Texas rig soft plastics. Crappie are in the shallow wood, but may slide out a little with the incoming front.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake LBJ fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on minnows in 12-16 feet of water on brush. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service. Bass are very good with catches up 6-8 pounds in the grass with chatterbaits, rattle traps and crankbaits. Bass are under the docks with ⅜ ounce jigs and frogs. Crappie are good with minnows over brush piles. Bass are good working docks and bulkheads with creature baits, worms and flukes.
reports.by: Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Martin Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are in pre-spawn pattern now. Crappie are fair to good but have scattered somewhat.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nacogdoches fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are excellent on medium diving, and small swimbaits in 12-16 feet of water. Crappie are excellent on brush piles and standing timber with white crappie jigs.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal’s ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Naconiche fishing report
reports.text: Some bass are being seen in deeper water in larger groups. Crappie population is good. Largemouth bass are excellent on Carolina rigs and small swimbaits 15 feet of water. Crappie are excellent on 1/16 ounce chartreuse or white crappie jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Navarro Mills fishing report
reports.text: Still no action for largemouth bass and white bass are slow. Crappie are good one day then slow the next.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O.H. Ivie fishing report
reports.text: A few bass can be caught suspended on jerkbaits up to 5 pounds this week over 25 feet of water. Crappie are fair in 30 feet of water suspended 10-15 feet down on main lake trees.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palestine fishing report
reports.text: Bass did slow down in the shallows, enough wind and clouds to move the shad back out a little.
reports.by: Jim Beggerly, Jim’s Fishing Lake Palestine

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Pinkston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are excellent on dropshot and small swimbaits in 16-20 feet of water. A lot of bass are 3-6 pounds. Crappie are poor on small white jigs.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal’s ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Sam Rayburn fishing report
reports.text: Bass are improving in shallow water where fish are chasing the bait into pockets. Crappie are slowly moving up the river.
reports.by: Captain Lynn Atkinson, Reel Um N Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tawakoni fishing report
reports.text: Swimbaits and slab spoons are working best. The largemouth bite has been good on plastics in 1-6 feet.
reports.by: Captain Michael Littlejohn, Lake Tawakoni Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texoma fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are showing up on brush and below docks. Bass fishing is good on plastics off the banks in 5–12 feet of water. Big bass will be looking for larger baits as the water cools off. Striped bass are excellent with daily limits on slabs under the birds.
reports.by: Jacob Orr, Lake Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Travis fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good and the bite is becoming stronger as the water temperature continues to cool. There is a really good topwater bass bite in the morning, but can last all day when there is wind. Bass are biting small swimbaits near grass, Wacky rig trick worms around the grass in 8-12 feet. Crappie are good under the docks on minnows. Bass are good chasing minnows in shallow coves.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tyler fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair under the boat houses with minnows. Bass are slow on trick worms and crankbaits. Crappie are good scattered on docks in 6-8 feet of water, or on the southern end of the lake chasing shad on minnows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Waco fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair with minnows and crappie jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Weatherford fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow. Crappie are fair in the crappie house on jigs or minnows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Alan Henry fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 30-40 feet on minnows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Amistad fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are fair on flukes, chatterbaits, rattle traps and soft plastics in 15-20 feet on main lake and secondary points.
reports.by: Captain Raul Cordero, Far West Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Athens fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good and can be caught on inside grass lines 4-8 feet with Texas rig worms, wacky rig senko and weightless flukes. Crappie are slow on small jigs over deep brush 25 feet. Report by Reagan Nelson, Lake Athens Bass Guide.
reports.by: Reagan Nelson, Lake Athens Bass Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bastrop fishing report
reports.text: Moving baits around the grass beds are producing some nice bass. Targeting rock piles and ledges with shaky heads and Carolina rigs will still catch numbers of bass.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bob Sandlin fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass bite is excellent. Spotted bass schooling around the dam has slowed. Windy banks and retaining walls should hold bass. Look for schooling bass, chasing shad.
reports.by: Blake Doughtie, Lake Country Lunkers Lures and Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bois d'Arc fishing report
reports.text: The top water action for bass has slowed down around pond weed, but still a few to catch. Bass are good in shallow pond dams and high spots with chatterbaits and square bills crankbaits. Crappie fishing is excellent in the main river channel timber and lower third of the lake in 30-50 feet of water catching crappie 6-28 feet down. Fish are very healthy with big black crappie being caught on jigs.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Braunig fishing report
reports.text: Bass are being caught around weeds and inside the weeds on plastics.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bridgeport fishing report
reports.text: Crappie have been slow, fish are scattered or holding tight to cover. A slab fished close to the bottom may draw a strike or two. Largemouth bass have been fair on crankbaits in the backs of creeks where there is clearer water.
reports.by: Keith Bunch, Lake Bridgeport Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brownwood fishing report
reports.text: Black bass to 4.50 pounds are excellent on buzz baits and swimbaits in the grass and weeds, or with crankbaits off the rocks in 5-10 feet around the rock cuts. Crappie are fair around docks 9 feet with brush on minnows or jigs and some off shore brush piles.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bryan fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are midlake suspended over deep water with most catches on minnows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Buchanan fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair on brush piles and standing timber in 20-25 feet of water with minnows. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service. Lake Buchanan bass fishing is great, and the colder the better on this lake.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Caddo fishing report
reports.text: We need some 30 degree nights to bring the temperatures down in the 50s to turn on the black bass in a feeding frenzy. Chatterbait, swimbait, trap or spinnerbait will work well on the main lake also when looking for bass around the grass as they will be feeding up pretty soon for the winter temps.
reports.by: Vince Richards, Caddo Lake Fishing & Fellowship

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Canyon Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are excellent on chatterbaits, crankbaits, wacky rigged senko over grass and hydrilla.

reports.title: Cedar Creek Lake fishing report

reports.by: Brent Herbeck, Herbeck’s Lonestar Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cisco fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on minnows. The bass are jumping, but no good reports.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Comanche Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Numbers of largemouth bass to 7 pounds are possible on soft plastics near elevation changes on the upper ends.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Conroe fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth are doing well on crankbaits and creature baits up to 25 feet. Crappie are in 13-21 feet on or near structure. Many folks are trolling with a deep diver and a pet spoon trailer, others are using slabs from Bradley Outdoors to jig for them, as well as casting swim baits or crank baits when schooled up.
reports.by: Brad Doyle with Bradley’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cooper fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good roaming in the river channel transitioning to the dam for the river pattern. Crappie are hitting minnows, jigs, or hand tied jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cypress Springs fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass bite is excellent. Spotted bass schooling around the dam has slowed.
reports.by: Blake Doughtie, Lake Country Lunkers Lures and Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Falcon fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are fair early or late in the day.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fayette fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good with numbers of catches but a majority of fish are undersized or yearlings.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fork fishing report
reports.text: The bass bite is slowing due to the cooler mornings, with water temperature 65 degrees. Black bass are sporadic around vegetation. The crappie fishing on Lake Fork is just phenomenal right now going into the early winter months. We are seeing some black crappie grouped up in numbers. The huge white crappie has been showing off the past month also.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Graham fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow biting on minows. Bass fishing is slow.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granbury fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are schooling with the sand bass. White and chartreuse jigging slabs are effective on the sand bass, striped bass and largemouth. Crappie action on submerged structures from Water’s Edge to the Peninsula are good on small jigs and minnows. Some good reports of largemouth bass on the upper ends in the river near laydowns on crankbaits and soft plastics.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granger fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are fair on black plastic worms fished around shallow cover. Crappie are slow on jigs fished in 8-16 feet of water.
reports.by: Tommy Tidwell, Tommy Tidwell’s Granger Lake Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Hawkins fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good with small poppers in baitfish patterns around shoreline brush and boat docks, and woolly buggers around hydrilla are a good bet.
reports.by: Guide Alex Guthrie, Fly Fish Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are being caught on riprap and cypress trees with grubs in the mornings and in 5-6 feet of water right to structure later in the day. Crappie are good right to structure as well being caught in small jigs and minnows in the rivers.
reports.by: Captain Zackary Scott, Zack Attack Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Jacksonville fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good on soft plastics and rattle traps around docks and 6-14 feet and on brush piles. Swimbaits and rattle traps will catch schooling bass.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Joe Pool Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are in the shallow wood, but may slide out a little with the incoming front.

reports.title: Lake O' the Pines fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass bite is excellent. Spotted bass schooling around the dam has slowed.
reports.by: Blake Doughtie, Lake Country Lunkers Lures and Guide Service

Crappie are good with minnows over brush piles. Bass are good working docks and bulkheads with creature baits, worms and flukes.
reports.by: Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lewisville fishing report
reports.text: White bass are fair on humps and points in 15-30 feet of water with slabs, jigs, and live bait. Crappie are fair in 6-26 feet of water. Bass are slow, with the most consistent bite in 2-6 feet of water slowly dragging soft plastics on a Texas rig or Ned rig.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Martin Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair to good on swimbaits, hybrid hunter, rattletraps and texas rigged worms around the hydrilla. Crappie are fair in brush piles in 15-20 feet using minnows and Bobby Garland black out jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Millers Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow. Crappie are fair in 14 feet of water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nacogdoches fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are excellent on medium diving chartreuse with a blue back crankbait, or Carolina rig on hard bottoms in deep water. Crappie are excellent in brush piles with white crappie jigs.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal’s ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nasworthy fishing report
reports.text: The bass bite has been fair on white chatterbait or spinnerbaits early morning and evening. Midday flipping soft plastics around reed bases in 1-3 feet of water is the ticket to catch shaded up largemouth bass. The key is to cover water until you find a good stretch that holds multiple bass. Crappie are good around boat docks on chartreuse jigs and catfish were fair on cut bait and stink bait around river channel bends.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Navarro Mills fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass and white bass are slow. Crappie are good in shallow water off of docks, with some catches in brush piles using minnows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O.H. Ivie fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are slow with catches up to 7 pounds. Crappie fare on main lake in deep Timber, minnows best with a few caught on small jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palestine fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing remains good, as the fish pursue shad that are moving into the creeks to the warmer water. 2 crappie hook and small minnows for the larger ones, or worms.
reports.by: Jim Beggerly, Jim’s Fishing Lake Palestine

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palo Pinto fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are slow.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Pinkston fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on small white jigs. Bass are good on dropshots and small swimbaits in 20 feet of water.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal’s ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Hubbard fishing report
reports.text: White bass later morning are on humps, levees and long points in 16-28 feet water using 3/4 ounce slabs. Crappie are good on brush in 18-28 feet on or off structure with minnows.
reports.by: John Varner, John Varner's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Somerville fishing report
reports.text: At Somerville marina the crappie bite is slow, bluegill are fair on crickets, worms, and catfish are fair on minnows and punch bait. Crappie are slow over brush in 8-16 feet of water with jigs and minnows. Black bass are slow on moving plastics in 6-12 feet of water.
reports.by: Weldon Kirk, Fish Tales Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tawakoni fishing report
reports.text: The fish look healthy and are giving a good fight in 5-25 feet swimbaits and slab spoons. The largemouth bite continues to improve.
reports.by: Captain Michael Littlejohn, Lake Tawakoni Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texoma fishing report
reports.text: Crappie fishing is picking up. Bass fishing will continue to improve as temperatures drop and water levels rise. Look for bass to be more active, chasing baits and making more mistakes. Use electronics to locate brush and structure bait will be holding on with bigger bass roaming the ledges. Striped bass are excellent with slabs and swimbaits along the ledges and drop-offs. Crappie are excellent on brush piles in 8-25 feet of water with the best bite on ⅛ ounce jig, and tipping the jig with minnows.
reports.by: Jacob Orr, Lake Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Toledo Bend fishing report
reports.text: Expect the bass to be good shallow with chatterbaits, small spinnerbaits and swimbaits. No reports on crappie.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Travis fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good and the bite is becoming stronger as the water temperature continues to cool. There is a really good topwater bass bite in the morning, but can last all day when there is wind. Bass are biting small swimbaits near grass, Wacky rig trick worms around the grass in 8-12 feet. Crappie are good under the docks on minnows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Twin Buttes fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair in deep brush with live minnows.
reports.by: Captain Michael Peterson, 4 Reel Fun Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tyler fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow in 20-25 feet of water with minnows. Bass are fair on topwater baits, crankbaits and spinnerbaits scattered throughout the lake. Crappie are good scattered on docks in 6-8 feet of water, or on the southern end of the lake chasing shad on minnows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Whitney fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair on small jigs and minnows in timber in 15-20 feet on the north end of the lake. Large mouth bass fishing is good around the docks.
reports.by: Captain Cory Vinson, Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Alan Henry fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair in 18-30 feet on minnows and jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Amistad fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are fair on buzzbaits, swimming jigs, square bill and rattle traps in 5-10 feet of water.
reports.by: Captain Raul Cordero, Far West Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Athens fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good on the inside grass lines in 5-8 feet with Texas rig worms and weightless flukes. Crappie are slow on small jigs over deep brush in 25 feet. Report by Reagan Nelson, Lake Athens Bass Guide.
reports.by: Reagan Nelson, Lake Athens Bass Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bastrop fishing report
reports.text: Lake Bastrop is a good place to go for bass. With high pressure lots of bass blowing up 3-5 feet in the reeds.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bob Sandlin fishing report
reports.text: Bass have been good around shallow docks with grass throwing shad colored bladed jigs, or finesse jigs in natural colors under docks. Big bass can be caught on a 6-7 inch line through swimbait, casting parallel to grass edges.
reports.by: Blake Doughtie, Lake Country Lunkers Lures and Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Braunig fishing report
reports.text: Bass are being caught in the weeds on plastics.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bridgeport fishing report
reports.text: Crappie continue to be good on minnows and jigs. Slabs fished close to the bottom, and around the structure will catch them. Largemouth bass are good on swimbaits and flat billed crankbaits.
reports.by: Keith Bunch, Lake Bridgeport Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brownwood fishing report
reports.text: Black bass to 6.50 pounds are excellent on Hag’s Jigs and swimbaits in the grass and weeds, or with crankbaits off the rocks in 5-10 feet around the rock cuts. Crappie are slow around docks with brush on minnows and some off shore brush piles.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Canyon Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are excellent in 2-8 feet of water in the grass with a white or green pumpkin chatterbait, and shad colored crankbaits.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Comanche Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Comanche Creek largemouth bass and catfish continue to be good to excellent. Black bass are being caught in numbers on soft plastics and crankbaits.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Conroe fishing report
reports.text: Bass are moving up shallow early and late. Crappie are in 13-21 feet of water on or close to structures. Many folks are trolling with a deep diver and a pet spoon trailer, others are using slabs from Bradley Outdoors to jig for them, as well as casting swim baits or crankbaits.
reports.by: Brad Doyle with Bradley’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cypress Springs fishing report
reports.text: Bass have been good around shallow docks with grass throwing shad colored bladed jigs, or finesse jigs in natural colors under docks. Big bass can be caught on a 6-7 inch line through swimbait, casting parallel to grass edges.
reports.by: Blake Doughtie, Lake Country Lunkers Lures and Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fork fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good on topwaters and small spinnerbaits. The crappie fishing on Lake Fork is just phenomenal right now going into the early winter months. You can find crappie almost everywhere on the lake but if you find the right area they are loaded up. We are seeing some black crappie grouped up in numbers. The huge white crappie has been showing off the past month also.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Graham fishing report
reports.text: Fishing is slow for crappie and bass due to the muddy water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granbury fishing report
reports.text: Sand bass are good on slabs and spinners on shallow humps and flats in 7-20 feet of water. Largemouth bass continue to be good in numbers with some good fish to 6lbs possible on main lake points and around creek entrances. Several largemouth bass have been caught on slabs while sand bass fishing.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Grapevine fishing report
reports.text: White bass are good feeding heavily so cast swimbaits, slabs or jigs.
reports.by: Omar Cotter, Luck O’the Irish Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth are great in water shallow on the main lake and cuts hitting worms and grubs, no weight rigged weedless. Crappie are fair hanging tight to structure in 8-16 fet of water.
reports.by: Captain Zackary Scott, Zack Attack Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Jacksonville fishing report
reports.text: Bass bite is tough in 8-20 feet on brush with soft plastics and swimbaits.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O' the Pines fishing report
reports.text: Bass have been good around shallow docks with grass throwing shad colored bladed jigs, or finesse jigs in natural colors under docks. Big bass can be caught on a 6-7 inch line through swimbait, casting parallel to grass edges.
reports.by: Blake Doughtie, Lake Country Lunkers Lures and Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake LBJ fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on chartreuse jigs and minnows in 12-20 feet of water on brush. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service. Bass are very good with catches up 6-8 pounds in the grass with chatterbaits, rattle traps and crankbaits. Bass are under the docks with ⅜ ounce jigs and frogs. Crappie are good with minnows over brush piles. Bass are good fishing docks and bulkheads with creature baits, worms and shallow crankbaits are catching most fish in 2-8 feet of water.
reports.by: Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Limestone fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are in 10-18 feet on offshore brush with minnows, or tight lining straight down in standing timber. Largemouth bass can be caught from 2-18 feet this week on docks, timber, bulkheads, rocks with Texas rigs, jigs, chatterbaits, and spinnerbait. Numbers of bass are still on offshore brush and roaming main lake points.
reports.by: Colan Gonzales, CG’s Just Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Livingston fishing report
reports.text: Lots of white bass in 7-15 feet of water using chartreuse and white Duck Tracker slabs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Martin Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good with swimbaits over the hydrilla along with wacky rigged worms. Crappie are fair to good in standing timber from 15-25 feet using minnows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Millers Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Lots of freshwater in the lake slowing the bass and hybrid bite. Bass are slow. Crappie are fair in 20 feet of water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Naconiche fishing report
reports.text: Some bass are being seen in deeper water in larger groups. Crappie population is good. Largemouth bass are excellent on small swimbaits or dropshots in 24 feet of water. Crappie are excellent for keeper sized fish biting white crappie jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Navarro Mills fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are slow. Crappie are good with some catches in brush piles, and off the dock with minnows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O.H. Ivie fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are slow with catches up to 6 pounds on a variety of shallow water baits. Crappie are fair in deeper trees on the main Lake near Ranger Cove. White bass are fair by the dam with slabs and rattle traps.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palestine fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are good in shallow water near the rising water level, then moving to a medium depth in 10 feet of water once sun rises. White crappie remain deep, so use live scopes to find them. Once you find the crappie they are hitting minnows and jigs. Back crappie are around rocks and concrete 6-22 feet of water with jigs.
reports.by: Jim Beggerly, Jim’s Fishing Lake Palestine

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Possum Kingdom fishing report
reports.text: Sand bass are still slow to fair in 20-30 feet of water with live shad or small slabs and jigs or rattle traps. Bass are moving up with the lake level rising. Report by JK Outdoors Bass Fishing Guide.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Roberts fishing report
reports.text: White bass can be caught on live bait and slabs in 15-25 feet. Crappie are still good in 5-20 feet on brush piles and small patches of structure with minnows. Crappie are shallow early then move deeper as the sun rises.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Richland Chambers fishing report
reports.text: Keep a slab and rattle trap tied on. Crappie bite fair in 10-15 feet of water.
reports.by: Royce Simmons, Gone Fishin' Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Somerville fishing report
reports.text: At Somerville marina the crappie bite is slow, bluegill and catfish are fair. Crappie are slow over brush in 8-16 feet of water with jigs and minnows. Black bass are slow on moving plastics in 6-12 feet of water.
reports.by: Weldon Kirk, Fish Tales Guide Service.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texoma fishing report
reports.text: Crappie fishing is picking up. Bass fishing will continue to improve as temperatures drop and water levels rise. Look for bass to be more active, chasing baits and making more mistakes. Use electronics to locate brush and structure bait will be holding on with bigger bass roaming the ledges. Birds will lead the way to feeding striped bass then cast slabs beneath.
reports.by: Jacob Orr, Lake Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Travis fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good with active fish up shallow, so throwing lures such as shallow crankbaits, hard and soft jerkbaits and topwaters will get some of those bass. Really good topwater bass bite in the morning, but lasts all day when there is wind. Bass are biting small swimbaits near grass, Wacky rig trick worms around the grass in 8-12 feet. Crappie are good under the docks on minnows. Bass are hitting small shallow crankbaits and medium diving crankbaits fished around rock and brush points.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Twin Buttes fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow and small, with undersized fish scattered in 7-15 feet of water with minnows. Some crappie are transitioning from brush to deeper areas but the big winter move is yet to come.
reports.by: Captain Michael Peterson, 4 Reel Fun Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Waco fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good with fish scattered throughout the lake.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Weatherford fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow in shallow water on swimbaits and spinnerbaits. Small crappie are fair with fish suspended in open water near brush piles with jigs and minnows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Alan Henry fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair in 30-40 feet on minnows and jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Amistad fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are good in 5-15 feet on secondary points and the back of bigger bays with deep water access.
reports.by: Captain Raul Cordero, Far West Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Athens fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good on the inside of grass lines with Texas rig worms and weightless flukes. Crappie are slow on small jigs over deep brush 25 feet. Report by Reagan Nelson, Lake Athens Bass Guide.
reports.by: Reagan Nelson, Lake Athens Bass Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Austin fishing report
reports.text: Bass can be caught in the grass with flukes and divers, but the best bite is on worms.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bastrop fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good in the discharge with swimbaits, worms or a shaky head. Grass edges and reed edges are loaded up with bass, so cast a fluke, shad shaped swimbait, or a frog or wakebait. Bass can be caught on deep points and humps, or shallow by the reeds with senkos.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bob Sandlin fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are excellent in 10-20 feet on brush piles with jigs or minnows.
reports.by: Joey Crews, Lake Bob Sandlin Chubby Chaser Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bois d'Arc fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good throughout the day.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Braunig fishing report
reports.text: Bass are being caught along weed lines with plastics.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bridgeport fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are good on swimbaits and crankbaits. Crappie are good around shoreline docks and the 380 bridge. Chartreuse slabs have been best, but look for the deadstick bite to pick up as it gets colder.
reports.by: Keith Bunch, Lake Bridgeport Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brownwood fishing report
reports.text: Black bass to 8.70 pounds are excellent on Hag’s Jigs, frogs and swimbaits in the grass and weeds, with crankbaits off the rocks in 2-8 feet around the rock cuts. Crappie are slow with 10 inches catches around docks with brush on minnows in 15-18 feet and some offshore brush piles.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cisco fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are great on minnows. The bass are jumping, but no good reports.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Comanche Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Comanche Creek continues to produce unbelievable numbers of largemouth bass on soft plastics and crank baits near channel ledges and submerged tanks on the north ends.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Conroe fishing report
reports.text: Crappie have been fair at best with some being caught but the population just isn't great. Bass have been good on wind blown docks and points using crankbaits and green pumpkin plastics. Many folks are trolling with a deep diver and a pet spoon trailer, others are using slabs from Bradley Outdoors to jig for them, As well as casting swimbaits or crankbaits.
reports.by: Brad Doyle with Bradley’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fayette fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good on rattle traps and topwaters in the reeds.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fork fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good in shallow water early morning on topwaters around grass. Offshore bass are on mid range flats or first break line in 4-6 feet with square bill crankbaits and spinnerbaits. The crappie fishing on Lake Fork is just phenomenal right now going into the early winter months. You can find crappie almost everywhere on the lake but if you find the right area they are loaded up. We are seeing some black crappie grouped up in numbers. The huge white crappie has been showing off the past month also.
reports.by: Guide Alex Guthrie, Fly Fish Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granbury fishing report
reports.text: Best lure is a tail spinnerbait or jigging slab in white/chartreuse. Largemouth bass are being caught in numbers on soft plastics and crankbaits. Lots of smaller bass but many fish in the 3-6 pound range.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granger fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are fair on plastic worms fished up river around timber. Crappie are slow.
reports.by: Tommy Tidwell, Tommy Tidwell’s Granger Lake Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Grapevine fishing report
reports.text: White bass are good on swimbaits, slabs or jigs.
reports.by: Omar Cotter, Luck O’the Irish Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are really turning on with swimbaits and crankbaits in the shallows in the morning and switching to grubs and worms in the afternoons on structure. Crappie are fair, tight to structure in the creeks and rivers eating small jigs.
reports.by: Captain Zackary Scott, Zack Attack Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Hubbard Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair with a few three fish stringers over 10 pounds.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Jacksonville fishing report
reports.text: The best bass bite is on soft plastics around boat docks and brush piles.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lewisville fishing report
reports.text: Slabs, jigs, and live bait are working. Crappie are fair in 6 to 26 feet of water. Bass are best early morning or at sunset hitting jigs, spinnerbaits and crankbaits. Bass are cruising shallow cover eating shad or bluegill. Crappie are on deeper brush piles in 12-20 feet of water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Martin Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good fishing the hydrilla with weightless senkos and underspin swimbaits. Crappie have scattered somewhat, but schools can still be found in 15-25 feet around brush with minnows and Bobby Garland pintail jigs in S

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nacogdoches fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are good on Carolina rigs and deep diving crankbaits in 12-15 feet of water. Crappie are good white crappie jigs or live minnows.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal’s ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Naconiche fishing report
reports.text: Crappie population is good. Largemouth bass are excellent on small swimbaits or dropshots in 24 feet of water. Crappie are excellent for keeper sized fish biting white crappie jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O.H. Ivie fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are slow with catches up to 6 pounds. Crappie are good with some limits over the top of deeper trees on the main lake.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palo Pinto fishing report
reports.text: Crappie bite is nonexistent.
reports.by: David Holt, Lake Palo Pinto RV Park and Resort

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Pinkston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are good with small swimbaits or dropshots. Crappie are fair on white crappie jigs or live minnows.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal’s ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Possum Kingdom fishing report
reports.text: Look for them in 20-30 feet of water with live shad or small slabs and jigs or rattle traps. Bass are slow in 5-15 feet of water on ledges and points with chatterbaits, small crankbaits, and plastics. Report by JK Outdoors Bass Fishing Guide.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stamford fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow. Crappie are slow in shallow cattails.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stillhouse fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass fishing has been hit-or-miss with fish reorienting from hydrilla to sparse natural cover.
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tawakoni fishing report
reports.text: The best depth has been 5-15 feet on artificials including swim baits and slab spoons. The largemouth bite continues to improve.
reports.by: Captain Michael Littlejohn, Lake Tawakoni Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texana fishing report
reports.text: Bass and crappie are slow due to weather and lower lake elevation.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texoma fishing report
reports.text: Crappie fishing is picking up near docks and on brush. Use jigs tipped with a crappie nibble, using electronics to locate active fish. Crappie are still roaming near structures, with many sitting on the bottom of the brush. Bass fishing will improve with recent rainfall and inflow. Follow the birds and cast slabs beneath for limits of fish.
reports.by: Jacob Orr, Lake Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Toledo Bend fishing report
reports.text: Shallow bass are still best with swim jigs, swimbaits, topwater, and frogs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Travis fishing report
reports.text: There is a good topwater bass bite due to the cooler morning temperatures. Bass are also feeding around the grass, so cast a Texas-rigged soft plastic like a worm, craw or jig.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Walter E. Long fishing report
reports.text: Fall conditions are in full effect and bass are chasing shad so they can be caught with multiple moving techniques like swimbaits, spinnerbaits, crankbaits and jerkbaits off the reed line and in the open flats and points.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Weatherford fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair in shallow water on swimbaits and spinnerbaits. Crappie are fair in 18-20 feet of water on brush piles with jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Whitney fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair on small jigs and minnows in timber in 15-20 feet on the north end of the lake. Largemouth bass fishing is good around the docks.
